body.statement: Let \(C\) be a fixed full-row-rank real matrix whose first row is \(\mathbf 1^\top\), and let \(G(b)=\{x\in\mathbb R^k:Cx=b,\ x\ge0\}\).  Over all right-hand sides whose first coordinate is one and whose fiber is nonempty, there is a finite constant \(H(C)\) such that \(e_1(G(b'),G(b))\le H(C)\|b'-b\|_1\).  A valid upper constant is computable from the finitely many full-row-rank active submatrices of the equality-plus-nonnegativity system (equivalently, after replacing each equality by two inequalities).

source.locator: Sections 2--3, feasible-solution Lipschitz constants for a perturbed linear program
